title: La hora
goal: Tell the time, say when in the day things happen and describe your daily routine.

lessons.title: What time is it?
lessons.notes:
**¿Qué hora es?** For one o'clock it's singular: **Es la una**. For every other hour it's plural: **Son las dos, son las tres...** (las horas, feminine plural).
Add minutes with **y** up to half past, and take them away with **menos** after it:
**Son las cuatro y cuarto** (4:15) · **Son las cuatro y media** (4:30) · **Son las cinco menos cuarto** (4:45 - 'five minus a quarter')
**Son las ocho y diez** (8:10) · **Son las nueve menos veinte** (8:40)
Timetables use the 24-hour clock (las 18:30 = las dieciocho treinta). Politely asking a stranger: **¿Tiene hora?**

items.note: son las dos = it's two o'clock

sentences.en: Excuse me, have you got the time?
accept_en: Excuse me, do you have the time?
Sorry, do you know the time?

sentences.es: El carro llega en diez minutos.
sentences.en: The car arrives in ten minutes.
accept_en: The car is arriving in ten minutes.
The car will be here in ten minutes.

lessons.title: Morning, afternoon, night
lessons.notes:
**La mañana** (the morning) and **mañana** (tomorrow) are the same word - the article tells you which. 'Tomorrow morning' is **mañana por la mañana**.
Parts of the day:
**por la mañana / por la tarde / por la noche** = in the morning / afternoon / at night (when, in general)
**de la mañana / de la tarde / de la noche** = with a clock time: **a las siete de la mañana** (7 am), **a las diez de la noche** (10 pm)
Much of Latin America also says **en la mañana**. **Antes** = before, earlier; **después** = after, afterwards.

accept_en: I study Spanish in the evening.

sentences.es: La clase es a las seis de la tarde.
sentences.en: The class is at six in the evening.
accept_en: The lesson is at six in the evening.

sentences.es: Llego a las siete de la mañana.
sentences.en: I arrive at seven in the morning.
accept_en: I get there at seven in the morning.

sentences.es: Por la tarde camino en la playa.
sentences.en: In the afternoon I walk on the beach.
accept_en: I walk on the beach in the afternoon.
Before that, I have a coffee.

sentences.es: Son las diez de la noche.

lessons.title: Meals and the working day
lessons.notes:
Each meal has a noun and a matching -ar verb:
**el desayuno → desayunar** (breakfast / to have breakfast)
**el almuerzo → almorzar** (lunch / to have lunch)
**la cena → cenar** (dinner / to have dinner)
So you don't 'have' a meal in Spanish, you 'breakfast' and 'dine': **Desayuno a las siete. Cenamos a las ocho.**
Almorzar changes o → **ue** when stressed: **almuerzo, almuerzas** (more in unit 15). In Spain and Mexico **la comida** is the big midday meal.
**Salir** (to go out, leave) is regular except **salgo** (I leave): **Salgo de casa a las ocho.**

sentences.es: Salgo de casa a las ocho.
accept_en: I leave the house at eight.

accept_en: I eat lunch at the office.

accept_en: I finish my work at five.

accept_en: I go back home in the afternoon.
I get home in the evening.

accept_en: We eat dinner at eight in the evening.

sentences.es: El almuerzo es a la una.

sentences.en: I'm not going out today, I'm tired.
accept_en: I'm not going out today, I am tired.

sentences.en: What time do you have breakfast?

lessons.title: A typical day
lessons.notes:
To tell your day as a story, line it up with sequence words: **primero** (first), **luego** / **después** (then, after that), **más tarde** (later), **por último** (finally).
**Primero desayuno, luego trabajo y por último ceno con mi familia.**
**Ver** (to see, to watch) is regular except **veo** (I see): veo, ves, ve, vemos, ven. Latin America uses **ver** more than mirar for watching TV: **Veo una serie.** A person you see takes a little **a**: **Veo a Ana** (more in unit 14).
**Luego** is also in **hasta luego** - 'until later'.

sentences.en: First I have breakfast, then I work.
accept_en: First I eat breakfast, then I work.
Later on I watch a show.
Later I watch a TV series.

sentences.es: Por último, ceno con mi familia.
sentences.en: Finally, I have dinner with my family.
accept_en: Lastly, I have dinner with my family.

sentences.es: Después del trabajo, estoy en el gimnasio.
sentences.en: After work, I'm at the gym.
accept_en: After work I am at the gym.
After work, I'm in the gym.

sentences.es: Veo una película por la noche.
sentences.en: I watch a film at night.
accept_en: I watch a movie in the evening.

sentences.es: Normalmente veo la televisión con mi esposa.
sentences.en: I normally watch TV with my wife.
accept_en: I usually watch television with my wife.

sentences.en: Do you watch series in Spanish?
accept_en: Do you watch shows in Spanish?

sentences.es: Luego tomo un café con Ana.
sentences.en: Then I have a coffee with Ana.
accept_en: Later I have a coffee with Ana.

sentences.es: Primero estudio y más tarde veo a mis amigos.
sentences.en: First I study and later I see my friends.
